prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many app sessions did the users of each account have in October 2025? Use only the app events from 1 to 31 October 2025 (UTC days of event_ts), so a user's first event in October starts a session. A user's first app event starts a session, and an event more than 30 minutes after the same user's previous event starts a new one; an event exactly 30 minutes later stays in the same session. Measure each gap as the time between the two moments in event_ts, a UTC instant, never between clock times. Return two columns, in this order: account_id and sessions. Return one row for each account with app events in October. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which rows LAG compares: each gap must come from the same user's previous event.
Without a partition, the row before can belong to another user of another account, so two users' events look like one session.
starter_sql:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event in October 2025
  SELECT user_id, account_id, event_ts,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-10-01 00:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-01 00:00:00+00'
), flagged AS (
  -- one row per app event in October 2025
  SELECT user_id, account_id, event_ts,
    CASE WHEN prev_ts IS NULL OR event_ts - prev_ts > INTERVAL '30 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session
  FROM gaps
)
SELECT account_id, SUM(new_session) AS sessions
FROM flagged
GROUP BY account_id
why_this_works: PARTITION BY user_id makes LAG read each user's own previous event, so another user's activity never joins a session.
